explain.say: On International Women's Day in February 1917, women textile workers in Petrograd walked out shouting for bread. Within days, hundreds of thousands were on the streets, and soldiers joined them. Tsar Nicholas the Second gave up his throne, ending three centuries of Romanov rule. Look at the timeline of one extraordinary year.

explain.say: Why did the monarchy collapse so fast? See the causes. Russia had lost millions of men in the war, cities ran short of bread and fuel, and the tsar had taken personal command of the army in 1915, so defeats became his fault. The key moment came when soldiers refused to fire on the crowds. Which cause would make a soldier change sides?

explain.say: Now two powers shared Russia. See the comparison. The Provisional Government, later led by Alexander Kerensky, had authority but kept fighting the war and delayed giving land to peasants. The Petrograd Soviet, a council of workers and soldiers, controlled the army units. Historians call this dual power. Which side held the guns?

Look at the map. In April 1917 Germany let Lenin travel from Switzerland in a sealed train, hoping he would take Russia out of the war. He demanded all power to the soviets, promising peace, land and bread. In October his Bolsheviks seized the Winter Palace in Petrograd with little bloodshed. Why would Germany help a revolutionary?

Then power narrowed: the Bolsheviks closed the elected Constituent Assembly in January 1918, where they had about a quarter of the vote, and civil war followed. Richard Pipes saw a coup; Alexander Rabinowitch and Sheila Fitzpatrick saw a party riding popular radicalism. Great work. Challenge: argue that both views can be partly right.

faq.q: Why did the tsar fall in 1917?
faq.a: Heavy war losses, food and fuel shortages in the cities, the tsar's unpopular leadership and long-standing grievances led to mass protests in Petrograd in February 1917. When the soldiers joined the crowds, Nicholas II abdicated.

faq.q: How did the Bolsheviks take power?
faq.a: The Provisional Government grew weak by continuing the war and delaying land reform. The Bolsheviks won majorities in the Petrograd and Moscow soviets, and on 25 October 1917, old style, their Red Guards and soldiers seized the Winter Palace and key points in Petrograd.

The uneasy sharing of power between the Provisional Government and the Petrograd Soviet from March to October 1917. The government had official authority, but the Soviet controlled many soldiers and workers.
Lenin's programme on returning in April 1917: no support for the Provisional Government, an end to the war, land to the peasants and all power to the soviets.

faq.q: Was the October Revolution a coup or a popular revolution?
faq.a: Richard Pipes saw it as a coup by a small party. Social historians such as Alexander Rabinowitch and Sheila Fitzpatrick showed widespread radicalism among workers and soldiers that the Bolsheviks used. Many historians see elements of both.

facts: Nicholas II abdicated in March 1917, early March in the old Russian calendar.
The Bolsheviks seized power on 25 October 1917 old style, 7 November in the modern calendar.
The Treaty of Brest-Litovsk with Germany was signed in March 1918.
